text: Two Fire page corrections: a nearby evacuation order no longer reads as “all clear” for our hill, and a failed earthquake check no longer counts as “nothing to report”
All six sections now fit the top of a phone screen — Weather, Living Here, Events and HOA used to be hidden behind a sideways swipe — plus bigger buttons and clearer text throughout
Fire page fixes: a shelter-in-place order now says stay inside (never “leave now”), an evacuation warning for our zone always leads, and the quiet-day summary can no longer sit on top of a real alert
Two neighborhood events are up — Burgers & Brews for the dads (Sat, Oct 3) and the 2nd Annual Halloween Party (Sat, Oct 31), with flyers, prices and how to RSVP
When an outside data source stops answering, the site now shows everything else instead of sitting at “unknown”
Living Here shows the next trash pickup and Burrtec’s holiday schedule, and the home page flags weeks when pickup runs a day late
Weather alerts now say when they end (“Flood Advisory until 7 PM”), and the Fire page shows every NWS alert for our location
The site notices when it’s actually raining on our hill, the home page boxes are colour-coded like the status line, and that line now says “moderate” when the air is, not “good”
Easier on a phone — bigger text and buttons everywhere, Events opens on this week’s picks, and the Fire page puts evacuation info first when it matters
New Weather page, and air quality and fire weather now come from neighbor sensors right here on our hill — not a reading from six miles away
Easier to use with a keyboard or screen reader, and the emergency status line sits where “skip to content” can’t jump past it
The COC Performing Arts Center season is in Events, plus Living Here corrections — our schools, and where paint, batteries and propane actually go
Event days are now checked against the venue’s own page — the Old Town Newhall farmers market runs Saturdays, not Sundays
Trash day is Tuesday (now on Living Here), plus a decluttering pass so quiet days show less and the important things stand out
“Smell smoke but nothing listed?” — a first-20-minutes guide on the Fire page, plus sharper warnings and easier-to-read colours
Real measured air quality from the EPA monitor in Santa Clarita, live power-outage tracking, and earthquake awareness
Neighborhood alerts — evacuation, fire and red-flag warnings auto-detected, with a one-tap WhatsApp share, plus AI-curated weekend picks every Friday
The home page leads with what’s coming up — live numbers, next events, and what’s new since your last visit
Local pros — a neighbor-shared solar & battery company on Living Here

Fires show acreage and containment from CAL FIRE with NASA satellite heat checks; Events got search and day-by-day grouping; and HOA & Resources explains your California homeowner rights in plain English
